agent.socket_path: Unix domain socket path for Rust↔Java agent IPC. (env: IBCTL_AGENT_SOCKET)
auth.paper.tws_userid: Paper account username. Set via env var, not in TOML. Must be empty (env-only) or an alphanumeric IB username. (env: TWS_USERID_PAPER)
auth.trading_mode: Trading mode: live | paper | both. Overrides deployment.tradingMode when set directly on runtime.auth. (env: TRADING_MODE)
auth.tws_userid: IB login username. Set via env var, not in TOML. Must be empty (env-only) or an alphanumeric IB username. (env: TWS_USERID)
command_server.allowed_commands: Action commands the command server accepts; any other action command is refused with "ERROR command not allowed by command_server.allowed_commands". One list for the live and paper instances, and the master switch for every caller: TCP clients, dashboard buttons and API tokens (the localhost-only rule for privileged commands still applies on top). Queries (STATUS, STATE, CONFIG, LOGS, WINDOWS, SUBSCRIBE) are always allowed and are not valid names here. Empty means the default, all of them. Listing too few can break tooling that sends the others (e.g. STOP and START from an approval flow). Env var accepts comma-separated form, e.g. SETRESTART,RECONNECTDATA. (env: IBCTL_ALLOWED_COMMANDS)
command_server.bind_address: TCP bind address for the command server.
command_server.control_from: IP allow-list for command access — CIDR-aware. Env var accepts comma-separated form. Empty locks out every client — schema rejects the empty case. (env: IBCTL_CONTROL_FROM)
command_server.enabled: Enable the IBC-compatible TCP command server (required for dashboard control). (env: IBCTL_COMMAND_SERVER_ENABLED)
command_server.paper_port: Paper instance command server TCP port.
command_server.port: Live instance command server TCP port. (env: IBCTL_COMMAND_PORT)
dashboard.enabled: Enable the web dashboard. Starts the entrypoint FastAPI when true. (env: IBCTL_DASHBOARD_ENABLED)
dashboard.external_url: External URL used to build ntfy action-button callback targets (e.g. https://ibctl.example.com). Leave empty if the dashboard is only reachable from inside the LAN and HITL ntfy_callback is unused. (env: IBCTL_DASHBOARD_EXTERNAL_URL)
dashboard.github_oauth_enabled: Enable GitHub OAuth login. Requires the IBCTL_GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID and IBCTL_GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET env vars (secrets are env-only). (env: IBCTL_GITHUB_OAUTH_ENABLED)
dashboard.notifications_enabled: Enable notifications (ntfy, Slack, Telegram). Requires dashboard.enabled. (env: IBCTL_NOTIFICATIONS_ENABLED)
dashboard.oidc_enabled: Enable generic OIDC/SSO login (Authentik, Keycloak, etc.). Requires IBCTL_OIDC_CLIENT_ID, IBCTL_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET, and oidcIssuer. (env: IBCTL_OIDC_ENABLED)
dashboard.scheduled_restart_grace_minute: When an outage starts at a scheduled restart (the daily auto restart or the weekly cold restart), minutes to hold the first "session down" alert while the Gateway comes back on its own. 0 = no grace. (env: IBCTL_SCHEDULED_RESTART_GRACE_MINUTES)
dashboard.session_down_alert_minutes: Minutes a mode's API session has to stay down before the dashboard sends a "session down" alert. 0 turns the alert off. (env: IBCTL_SESSION_DOWN_ALERT_MINUTES)
dashboard.session_down_renag_minutes: Minutes between repeat "still down" alerts while the session stays down. 0 sends one alert per outage. (env: IBCTL_SESSION_DOWN_RENAG_MINUTES)
dashboard.session_idle_minutes: Minutes without any user activity before a dashboard login ends and the person has to sign in again. 0 turns the idle logout off; the 7-day limit on every session still applies. Applies to the password login and to GitHub OAuth / OIDC alike. The page's own background refreshes don't count as activity, so an open tab left alone does time out. API tokens are not sessions and are not affected. A value outside 0..1440 is a preflight error. (env: IBCTL_SESSION_IDLE_MINUTES)
dashboard.token: The dashboard password, used only by the login form. It is not a Bearer token and not an HTTP Basic password; API clients use named API tokens, created and revoked on the dashboard's API access page. Empty = no password login (set GitHub OAuth or OIDC instead, or the dashboard stays read-only). Secrets never go in TOML: set the actual password via IBCTL_DASHBOARD_TOKEN. The schema enforces length == 0 (env-only). (env: IBCTL_DASHBOARD_TOKEN)
dashboard.version_probe_client_id: API client ID the weekly Gateway version check connects with. If it's in use it tries the next 7, so keep ID..ID+7 clear of your own API clients. (env: IBCTL_VERSION_PROBE_CLIENT_ID)
dashboard.zmq_enabled: ZMQ PUB socket for external status subscribers. On by default when the dashboard is running; set false to disable. (env: IBCTL_ZMQ_ENABLED)
dashboard.zmq_port: ZMQ PUB socket TCP port. (env: IBCTL_ZMQ_PORT)
gateway.java_heap_size: JVM heap size in MB. Must be >= 64 or the JVM refuses to launch. (env: JAVA_HEAP_SIZE)
gateway.live_api_port: Gateway API port for live trading (Gateway listens here; default 4001). Paired with liveSocatPort which fronts external clients.
gateway.live_socat_port: Socat forwarding port for live (external-facing; default 4003). External clients connect here; socat forwards to liveApiPort.
gateway.paper_api_port: Gateway API port for paper trading (Gateway listens here; default 4002).
gateway.paper_socat_port: Socat forwarding port for paper (external-facing; default 4004).
gateway.time_zone: IB Gateway's own session time zone. Empty means ibctl leaves the Gateway's jts.ini alone and only reports the zone in use. When set, ibctl writes it into the `[Logon] TimeZone` line of the mode's jts.ini before every Gateway launch and checks it after login. `time_zone_live` / `time_zone_paper` override `time_zone` for that mode. This is separate from the container's `TZ`, which only sets the clock zone of the container and the JVM. (env: TIME_ZONE)
gateway.time_zone_live: Gateway session time zone for live mode; overrides `time_zone` when set. An IANA name such as America/New_York, or empty. See `time_zone`. (env: TIME_ZONE_LIVE)
gateway.time_zone_paper: Gateway session time zone for paper mode; overrides `time_zone` when set. An IANA name such as America/New_York, or empty. See `time_zone`. (env: TIME_ZONE_PAPER)
gateway.tws_major_vrsn: Gateway/TWS major version. Auto-detected from the installation if empty. (env: TWS_MAJOR_VRSN)
gateway.tws_path: Path to the TWS/Gateway installation directory. (env: TWS_PATH)
gateway.tws_settings_path: Settings storage path; empty = use twsPath. The recovery-marker persistence layer writes here — ensure Jts_live and Jts_paper live on a persistent volume. (env: TWS_SETTINGS_PATH)
ib_status.kick_active_session: When the dashboard pushes IBSTATUS=unavailable, should ibctl interrupt an already-authenticated session? Default: false. IBSTATUS was designed as a retry-gate — if IBKR backends are unreachable, don't hammer them with login attempts. It was never meant to kill active sessions. The scraper can be wrong (CDN blips, slow page updates) and Gateway's own UI label is the authoritative "my session is healthy" signal — detected via label inspection in the revocation bus, not via the public status page. Set to true only to restore the historical behavior where any unavailable push transitions Connected → WaitingForIB. Only useful if you trust the scraper more than the Gateway UI label. Preflight enforces a live-mode guard: kickActiveSession=true combined with deployment.tradingMode in {"live","both"} raises unless IBCTL_KICK_LIVE_SESSION_OK=1.
ib_system_status.backend_hosts: IB backend servers to reach via TCP probe as a liveness signal.
ib_system_status.check_interval_seconds: Seconds between IB status page scrapes. Default 300 (5 min). (env: IB_STATUS_CHECK_INTERVAL)
ib_system_status.enabled: Enable IB system status monitoring (requires dashboard.enabled). (env: IBCTL_IB_STATUS_ENABLED)
ib_system_status.extra_benign_phrases: Additional benign phrases appended to the built-in list — alerts matching these are treated as non-blocking (e.g. "is resolved").
ib_system_status.extra_blocking_keywords: Additional blocking keywords appended to the built-in list — alerts matching these are forced to CRITICAL severity (e.g. "emergency").
ib_system_status.extra_exchange_keywords: Additional exchange keywords appended to the built-in list — alerts mentioning any of these are treated as non-blocking (e.g. "PAXOS,COINBASE").
ib_system_status.fallback_host: CDN fallback host for the internet-connectivity ping check.
ib_system_status.region: Region filter for maintenance windows: "NA" | "EU" | "APAC". (env: IB_STATUS_REGION)
ib_system_status.ttl_seconds: Fail-open TTL: if no status update arrives within this period, assume IB is available. Prevents stale-scraper false negatives.
logging.futures_session_logging: Use futures market session dates for log filenames instead of calendar dates. When true, log files roll at sessionReopenHour ET (default 18 = 6 PM); when false, files roll at midnight local time. (env: IBCTL_FUTURES_SESSION_LOGGING)
logging.log_dir: Directory for persistent log files; empty = stdout only (no file logging). (env: IBCTL_LOG_DIR)
logging.retention_days: Days of daily log files to keep, today included; older files are deleted by the dashboard (at start, then every 6 hours) for ibctl and the dashboard alike. 0 keeps everything. (env: IBCTL_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS)
logging.session_reopen_hour: Hour (0-23, US/Eastern) when the futures session reopens and the next trading day's log file begins. Only used when futuresSessionLogging = true. Default 18 (6 PM ET — CME futures reopen). (env: IBCTL_SESSION_REOPEN_HOUR)
session.tws_cold_restart: Cold restart time in "HH:MM" 24h format (e.g., "09:00"). Empty = disabled. Schema-enforced format — hand-edits that violate it are rejected at Pkl eval. (env: TWS_COLD_RESTART)
session.tws_cold_restart_day: Cold restart day of week: 0=Sunday, 1=Monday, ..., 6=Saturday. Default 0 (Sunday). (env: TWS_COLD_RESTART_DAY)
site.auto_launch: Auto-launch Gateway on container startup. Rendered under `[site].auto_launch`. A standby node with auto_launch=true is an HA split-brain foot-gun: two nodes race the same IB session. Preflight has an IBCTL_STANDBY_AUTO_LAUNCH_OK=1 escape hatch for niche hot-standby setups. (env: IBCTL_AUTO_LAUNCH)
site.role: Site role for HA topologies: primary | standby. Rendered under `[site].role`. (env: IBCTL_SITE_ROLE)
timing.agent_tick_ms: Java agent-side delay after each Swing action (ms).
timing.api_port_probe_fails_before_revok: Consecutive TCP probe failures before firing ApiPortListenerLost revocation. Absorbs transient OS-level blips. Range: 1..=10. (env: IBCTL_API_PORT_PROBE_FAILS_BEFORE_REVOKE)
timing.api_port_probe_interval_secs: TCP probe interval to Gateway's API port during post-auth states. Ground-truth check for "is Gateway actually listening?" — independent of Swing UI labels. 0 = disabled (rely on label probe only). Range: 0 | 1..=3600 seconds. (env: IBCTL_API_PORT_PROBE_INTERVAL_SECS)
timing.jvm_shutdown_timeout_secs: Seconds to wait for JVM graceful shutdown (SIGTERM) before escalating to SIGKILL.
timing.login_dialog_timeout_secs: Seconds to wait for the login window to appear before giving up. 0 = wait indefinitely (useful for headless servers during IB maintenance). Default 120. This field intentionally allows 0 — see doc. (env: IBCTL_LOGIN_TIMEOUT)
timing.login_radio_delay_ms: Pause after clicking login radio buttons (IB API, Paper Trading) (ms).
timing.popup_max_wait_secs: Max seconds to wait for popups before moving on.
timing.popup_quiet_secs: Seconds of no popups before considering login complete (quiet threshold).
timing.post_login_delay_ms: Wait after clicking login button before checking for 2FA (ms).
timing.recovery.backoff_interval_secs: Sleep between Backoff retries (seconds). Default 900 (15 min). (env: IBCTL_RECOVERY_BACKOFF_INTERVAL_SECS)
timing.recovery.enabled: master enable — set false in TOML to disable the coordinator entirely without touching env. Env IBCTL_RECOVERY_DISABLED=1|true|yes wins if set. Default true.
timing.recovery.fingerprint_streak_forci: same-error streak forcing HITL — skips time-based escalation and enters HITL immediately when the same error fingerprint recurs. Default 8 (~40 min at 5-min cycles). (env: IBCTL_RECOVERY_FINGERPRINT_STREAK)
timing.recovery.giveup_alert_resend_inte: Minimum wall-clock interval before re-firing a give-up alert while the state machine is still parked in GivenUp (hours). Default 6. (env: IBCTL_RECOVERY_GIVEUP_ALERT_RESEND_INTERVAL_HOURS)
timing.recovery.giveup_callback_valid_ho: Signed retry-link validity window on the give-up alert (hours, 1..=168). Default 12 (matches the HITL 2FA callback convention). (env: IBCTL_RECOVERY_GIVEUP_CALLBACK_VALID_HOURS)
timing.recovery.giveup_ntfy_kind: Coalescer key for the give-up ntfy alert. Distinct kind lets the dashboard's ntfy coalescer dedupe re-fires within the resend interval.
timing.recovery.min_success_dwell_secs: Minimum Connected dwell to count as a success and reset the phase timer. Default 60. Guards against a 3-second flap-Connect resetting the timer indefinitely — the exact pathology this coordinator is meant to detect. (env: IBCTL_RECOVERY_MIN_SUCCESS_DWELL_SECS)
timing.relogin_failure_action: Action after exhausting re-login attempts. "reauth" — re-use the existing login form without killing the JVM (default) "restart" — kill and relaunch the JVM for a clean slate (env: IBCTL_RELOGIN_FAILURE_ACTION)
timing.relogin_max_attempts: Max re-login attempts before cancelling and restarting the JVM. On first attempt, waits 30s then clicks Re-login; if it fails again (up to this limit), clicks Cancel and takes reloginFailureAction. 0 = always cancel. Default 1. (env: IBCTL_RELOGIN_ATTEMPTS)
timing.restart_delay_secs: Seconds to wait before restarting the JVM after an error or failure. Gives Gateway time to self-recover from transient connection losses. Default 90. (env: IBCTL_RESTART_DELAY)
timing.ui_tick_ms: Delay between UI actions in the config dialog (ms).
twofa.backoff.callback_valid_hours: Hours the signed ntfy-action URL stays valid — one-shot, redeemed on first successful click. Range 1..=168 (one week ceiling). (env: IBCTL_TWOFA_CALLBACK_VALID_HOURS)
twofa.backoff.cold_restart_preempts_hitl: Does a scheduled cold restart preempt WaitingForHitl2fa? true — cold restart wins; exit HITL, run restart, re-enter login (default) false — cold restart deferred until HITL exits via its normal path (env: IBCTL_TWOFA_COLD_RESTART_PREEMPTS_HITL)
twofa.backoff.counter_reset: Counter-reset policy after a successful reach of Connected. "any_reach" — reset as soon as Connected (default) "stable" — require Connected sustained for stableSecs before reset (env: IBCTL_TWOFA_COUNTER_RESET)
twofa.backoff.intervals_minutes: Retry cadence in minutes for periodic / both. Single value = constant. List = traverse then hold at last element. Must be non-empty for non- disabled strategies that include a timer. Elements must be > 0. (env: IBCTL_TWOFA_INTERVALS_MINUTES)
twofa.backoff.max_immediate_attempts: After this many failed 2FA rounds in a row, stop retrying and enter WaitingForHitl2fa. 0 = disabled (legacy behavior: loop forever). (env: IBCTL_TWOFA_MAX_IMMEDIATE_ATTEMPTS)
twofa.backoff.ntfy_send_retries: If the initial ntfy push fails (network blip, ntfy server down), how many times to retry the send on subsequent scheduled-retry wakeups. 0 = give up silently. Only meaningful when strategy includes ntfy_callback. (env: IBCTL_TWOFA_NTFY_SEND_RETRIES)
twofa.backoff.on_timeout: What a failed 2FA round leads to. The names date from when a timer ended rounds and relaunched the JVM; retries now stay in the running Gateway. "restart_then_hitl" — retry the login; HITL once maxImmediateAttempts rounds failed (default) "restart_forever" — never park (retry after every failed round) "hitl_immediately" — the first failed round goes straight to HITL unattendedHours outranks all three. (env: IBCTL_TWOFA_ON_TIMEOUT)
twofa.backoff.stable_secs: Seconds Connected must persist before resetting the attempt counter when counterReset = "stable". Ignored for "any_reach". (env: IBCTL_TWOFA_STABLE_SECS)
twofa.backoff.strategy: HITL resume strategy: "disabled" | "periodic" | "ntfy_callback" | "both". "disabled" = stay in HITL forever (dashboard still reflects state; operator must send HITL_RESUME manually via dashboard). (env: IBCTL_TWOFA_STRATEGY)
twofa.backoff.unattended_hours: Hours nobody answers an IB Key push: "HH:MM-HH:MM" in the container's time zone (TZ), may wrap midnight; "" or "off" = none. A 2FA round that fails inside them parks in WaitingForHitl2fa with the Gateway kept running, instead of sending another push. It stays parked until the operator's Retry or the Sunday re-auth: no HITL auto-retry fires inside the window, and none fires because it ended. (env: IBCTL_TWOFA_UNATTENDED_HOURS)
twofa.device: 2FA device name for the device selection dialog. Empty = skip selection. (env: TWOFA_DEVICE)
twofa.exit_interval: Seconds an IB Key push may go unanswered before ibctl says it is waiting. It never ends the round: the Gateway does, by closing its prompt; a prompt still open after 30 min is cancelled. Also bounds the wait for the challenge after the device picker closes. Named after IBC's SecondFactorAuthenticationExitInterval, IBC's wait AFTER the prompt closes. Rust code default is 180; base.pkl overrides to 120 for Docker deployment. (env: TWOFA_EXIT_INTERVAL)
twofa.provider: TOTP provider: "oathtool" (shells out) or "builtin" (not yet implemented). (env: TOTP_PROVIDER)
twofa.relogin_after_timeout: Force re-login even after a 2FA timeout — overrides timeoutAction=restart semantics when set. (env: RELOGIN_AFTER_TWOFA_TIMEOUT)
twofa.secret_env: Name of the env var holding the TOTP shared-key value used to generate 2FA codes. Field stores the *env var name*, never the credential itself. This is the *name* of an env var — not the secret value itself.
twofa.timeout_action: What a failed 2FA round does: "restart" (retry the login as `backoff` says, in the running Gateway) or "exit" (shut ibctl down). (env: TWOFA_TIMEOUT_ACTION)
ui.connectivity.ib_page_reachable: IB status page reachable — the scraper's ground-truth check succeeded.
ui.connectivity.ib_page_unreachable: IB status page unreachable — cannot fetch the scraper's ground-truth signal.
ui.connectivity.internet_connected: Internet connected — this host can reach the public network.
ui.connectivity.internet_disconnected: Internet disconnected — this host cannot reach the public network.
ui.controls.reconnect_account: Reconnect to IB. Presses Ctrl+Alt+R in the Gateway, which re-opens its connection to IB's servers. It asks the Gateway to simulate a disconnect, so the session link drops briefly.
ui.controls.reconnect_data: Reconnect market data feeds. Presses Ctrl+Alt+F in the Gateway, which drops and re-opens its market-data connections. It asks the Gateway to simulate a disconnect, so data pauses for a few seconds.
ui.controls.restart_gateway: Restart the Gateway JVM. Kills the process and triggers a full re-authentication cycle including 2FA.
ui.controls.restart_socat: Restart the socat port forwarder. Kills and re-launches the TCP proxy that bridges the API port to the container interface.
ui.controls.start_gateway: Start a stopped Gateway. Only a Gateway waiting for START can be started; it launches and logs in again, with 2FA for LIVE.
ui.controls.stop_gateway: Stop the Gateway JVM and keep it stopped until Start. The Sunday cold restart leaves a stopped Gateway alone; a container restart or deploy launches it again.
ui.deployment_site.launch_policy: Launch policy — whether the Gateway auto-launches at boot or waits for a START command.
ui.deployment_site.role.primary: Primary site — launches the Gateway and holds the active IB session.
ui.deployment_site.role.standby: Standby site — stays warm, ready to promote if the primary goes down.
ui.deployment_site.site_role: Site role — primary or secondary; primary launches the Gateway, secondary stays warm.
ui.deployment_site.term: Deployment Site — role and launch policy of this host in the failover mesh.
ui.gateway.state_term: Gateway state — connection state reported by the Java Gateway process (Connected, Disconnected, etc.).
ui.health.error: Error — this component is unhealthy; operator action may be required.
ui.health.ok: Healthy — this component is operating normally.
ui.health.warning: Warning — this component is degraded or waiting; not blocking but worth watching.
ui.ib_status.status.available: IB backends are reachable and the status page reports no active outage.
ui.ib_status.status.maintenance: IB is in a scheduled maintenance window; sessions may be interrupted.
ui.ib_status.status.no_internet: This host has no internet connectivity — cannot reach IB or the status page.
ui.ib_status.status.scheduled: A maintenance window is scheduled within the near future.
ui.ib_status.status.unavailable: IB backends are reporting an active outage; login attempts will fail.
ui.ib_status.status.unknown: IB status page is unreachable — cannot tell the current backend health.
ui.recovery.phase.aggressive: Aggressive phase — retry every 30s to reconnect fast after a fresh outage.
ui.recovery.phase.backoff: Backoff phase — retry every 15min after aggressive reconnects fail.
ui.recovery.phase.given_up: Given up — recovery loop stopped after exhausting retries; operator intervention required.
ui.recovery.term: Recovery loop — background task that reconnects the Gateway after outages.
ui.trading_mode.both: Live + Paper — dual-instance deployment running both real and paper sessions side by side.
ui.trading_mode.live: Live trading mode — orders route to the real IB account.
ui.trading_mode.paper: Paper trading mode — orders route to the IB paper simulator account.
